1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6.name: Sicilian Defence: French Variation
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6.background: One of Black's three main replies to 2.Nf3, with 2...d6 and 2...Nc6. After 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 it leads to the Taimanov Variation, named after Mark Taimanov, and the Kan Variation, named after Ilya Kan and also called the Paulsen Variation after Louis Paulsen.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.d4.strategy: Offers the pawn trade that opens the game: after ...cxd4 White recaptures with a central knight and has open lines for both bishops and the queen, while Black gets a central pawn majority and a half-open c-file. White gets the initiative, Black the counterplay.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.c3.strategy: Prepares to build a full pawn centre with d4 and to keep it there, a calmer way to meet the Sicilian than the open play after an immediate d4. The price is the c3 square for the b1-knight; Black can strike back in the centre at once.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.c3.name: Sicilian Defence: Delayed Alapin Variation, with e6

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.Nc3.strategy: A waiting move: it develops, guards e4 and postpones d4 until Black shows which Sicilian it means to play. It mostly leads back into the usual open Sicilian, and the knight takes the square a c-pawn would want for a pawn centre.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.c4.strategy: Puts pawns on c4 and e4 so that d5 is covered twice, which holds back Black's freeing central break and gains space. White gives up the open play of d4 for a squeezing, positional game in which Black has to find room to breathe.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.c4.name: Sicilian Defence: Kramnik Variation

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.b3.strategy: Prepares to fianchetto the queen's bishop on the long diagonal and avoids the open Sicilian. It does nothing against Black's centre, though, and White's follow-up is unclear: Black is free to develop as it likes and to build a solid centre.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.b3.name: Sicilian Defence: French Variation, Westerinen Attack
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.b3.background: It is a rare independent try, occasionally played by Heikki Westerinen in the 1970s.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.b4.strategy: A deferred gambit: White offers the b-pawn to drag Black's c-pawn away and build a big pawn centre. Black can simply take it, and White gets little in return for the pawn; the idea is dubious.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.b4.name: Sicilian Defence: Wing Gambit Deferred

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.c3 d5.strategy: Strikes at e4 before White's pawn centre exists. The tension is resolved at once, White cannot enjoy the broad centre that c3 was preparing, and Black's pieces come out freely in an open game.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.c3 Nf6.strategy: Develops with an attack on e4, so White must either advance the pawn, gaining space but leaving a target, or defend it. Black keeps its choice of centre set-up open and makes White decide what to do with the e-pawn.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.d4 cxd4.strategy: Trades the c-pawn for White's d-pawn: Black gets a central pawn majority and a half-open c-file to work with. It costs time and hands White free development and open lines, the usual bargain of the open Sicilian.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.d4 a6.strategy: Spends a tempo on a6 before resolving the centre and prepares ...b5. Black has not yet taken on d4, so White can choose the pawn structure first.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.d4 a6.name: Sicilian Defence: Drazic Variation

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.d4 d5.strategy: Strikes in the centre at once, but opens the game before Black is developed. White takes the pawn, and a check with the bishop gains time, so Black is the one defending against a lead in development.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.d4 d5.name: Sicilian Defence: Marshall Counterattack

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.Nc3 a6.strategy: Takes b5 away from White's bishop and knights and prepares ...b5 for queenside space. Black waits to see whether White opens the centre with d4, in which case the play transposes into a normal Open Sicilian with the pawn already on a6.
